Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 3, 4, 14, 25, 32-39), as amended by Ley 19/2019, de 28 de noviembre (transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843) and Ley 18/2022, de 28 de septiembre (Crea y Crece); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de desarrollo de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 111/2021, de 23 de febrero, regulating the Registro de Titularidades Reales (arts. 3-4: UBO is any natural person with direct or indirect ownership or control exceeding 25%, or exercising control by other means); supervisory authority: SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias); SPAC listing overlay: Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de los Mercados de Valores y de los Servicios de Inversión and Reglamento (UE) 2017/1129 (prospectus regime).
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Restricted acceptance for a SPAC vehicle: a virtual administrative address is tolerated only where a genuine physical office in Spain exists in which management, corporate records, UBO files, and escrow documentation are available for on-site inspection; a pure virtual or registered-agent-only address fails the substance requirement of Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, art. 9) and would prevent notarial constitution and CNMV/BME admission to listing.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation); provincial Registro Mercantil at the registered office (deed registration); Notarial College via the Notario autorizante; CIRCE/DUE electronic incorporation window; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for tax identification.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC), especially Arts. 20-24 (notarial deed and bylaws), 58-62 (subscription and payment), 102-105 (single-member SL), 209-227 (administration and officers); Law 14/2013, of 27 September, on Support for Entrepreneurs (Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva).

Formation / constitutional filings

Certificación negativa de denominación social, Escritura Pública de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) with bylaws, registered in the Mercantile Registry, and NIF application using Modelo 036.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 90 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Standard SL requires share capital of at least EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in at incorporation and evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or an in-kind valuation report before the notary. If founders elect reduced capital of EUR 1 up to EUR 3,000, the company qualifies as a Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva, with mandatory allocation of 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve until EUR 3,000 is reached. No State escrow account is required; however, a SPAC depositary or trust escrow account at an eligible Spanish or EU credit institution is commercially mandatory and is evidenced to the notary and to the CNMV.

Funding & unlock path: Attestation of fire protection compliance under Royal Decree 513/2017; low-voltage installation certificate per Royal Decree 842/2002; structural load and occupancy clearance from the municipal architect; and a workplace risk-prevention service established under Law 31/1995 with annual occupational risk evaluation and health surveillance for office personnel.

Paid-in capital rule: Standard SL requires share capital of at least EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in at incorporation and evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or an in-kind valuation report before the notary. If founders elect reduced capital of EUR 1 up to EUR 3,000, the company qualifies as a Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva, with mandatory allocation of 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve until EUR 3,000 is reached. No State escrow account is required; however, a SPAC depositary or trust escrow account at an eligible Spanish or EU credit institution is commercially mandatory and is evidenced to the notary and to the CNMV.

Dirección General de Industria y PYME of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Tourism for industrial aspects; Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores for SPAC public-market authorization; and the Municipal Ayuntamiento for the local activity or opening licence.

Category: Autorización de admisión a negociación de valores en BME (CNMV listing authorization) and municipal 'Licencia de apertura y funcionamiento' for administrative offices.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – official portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

A non-resident entity without permanent establishment in Spain must appoint a Spanish tax representative (art. 10 bis LGT) and apply for an NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via AEAT form 036 or 036-equivalent digital procedure, presenting the foreign corporate registration certificate, apostilled/Apostille and translated bylaws, and evidence of the constitutional act. The AEAT assigns a non-resident NIF with a 'N' prefix for entities that are not established in Spain. For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the NIF is obtained at notarial incorporation and registration with the Mercantile Registry; the provisional NIF (prefixed 'C') becomes definitive upon filing form 600/036 before the Notary, with the final NIF format consisting of a letter, eight digits, and a control character.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A non-resident entity without permanent establishment in Spain must appoint a Spanish tax representative (art. 10 bis LGT) and apply for an NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via AEAT form 036 or 036-equivalent digital procedure, presenting the foreign corporate registration certificate, apostilled/Apostille and translated bylaws, and evidence of the constitutional act. The AEAT assigns a non-resident NIF with a 'N' prefix for entities that are not established in Spain. For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the NIF is obtained at notarial incorporation and registration with the Mercantile Registry; the provisional NIF (prefixed 'C') becomes definitive upon filing form 600/036 before the Notary, with the final NIF format consisting of a letter, eight digits, and a control character.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists. Tax classification is statutory: all Spanish-resident entities are subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at entity level. Available elections include: (i) group VIES registration and election to apply Spanish VAT Group Registration under art. 84.3 LIVA (for controlling companies with more than 50% holdings); (ii) election to file consolidated corporate tax returns under the special group regime (arts. 55-68 LIS); (iii) equity-holding entities (incl. SPACs) may elect treatment as pure holding companies, adjusting participation exemptions under the 95% dividend-and-capital-gains participation exemption (art. 21 LIS); (iv) hybrid mismatch elections under ATAD-derived rules are limited and subject to anti-deferral provisions (arts. 15bis, 23bis LGT). No discretionary pass-through election is available for an SL.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0 – no general VAT registration threshold in Spain. Any taxable person carrying out an economic activity in Spain must register before the start of supplies, regardless of turnover. Non-established taxable persons must register via AEAT form 036/037 or the non-EU procedure, subject to an interim registration deadline. An exception applies to intra-Community distance sales from another EU member state, where the €10,000 cross-border threshold triggers the obligation to register or use the One Stop Shop (OSS).

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods from Spain to third countries are subject to the 0% VAT rate (exempty with credit) under art. 21 LIVA, provided that the goods depart the EU customs territory and are transported by the seller or a third party on the seller's instructions. Services directly connected to export operations, international transport of goods, and ancillary services (loading, unloading, warehousing, and commissions) are eligible if evidenced. For a SPAC/blank-check entity, zero-rating typically applies only to genuine export transactions, not to financial or escrow fees; financial services are VAT-exempt without credit unless the 'international services' export condition is met. Beneficiary must be a non-EU taxable person or equivalent status, and the service must be for use outside the EU. Documentation must be retained for 4 years.

  • Customs Export Declaration – Single Administrative Document (DUA/SAD J.3) with proof of customs admission (electronic exit summary)
  • Commercial invoice in original
  • Packing list
  • Bill of Lading (origin sea), Air Waybill (air), or CMR waybill (road), showing Spain as departure and third country as destination
  • Proof of physical exit from EU customs territory (seal/release notification from the Spanish customs office)
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or evidence of payment from the non-EU buyer (when payment is received through banking rails)

B2B electronic invoicing is compulsory for all entrepreneurs and professionals under Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece'), with phased implementation commencing on 1 January 2025 for all taxable persons with annual turnover over €8 million, and by 1 January 2026 for others. The system requires digital invoices in structured formats (Facturae, XML, EDIFACT) interoperable with the receiving business. Additionally, the 'Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA' (SII) is mandatory for taxpayers in the large-enterprise regime (turnover over €6 million), VAT groups, and entities in select industries: they must transmit or register transaction records (invoices issued/received, intra-Community acquisitions, importations) to AEAT via web service/API within 4 calendar days from issuance/entry (8 calendar days for the general deadline), with a consolidated pre-evaluation period of 4 calendar days. There is no digital stamping or full real-time clearance in Spain; the SII operates as near-real-time record submission without prohibition of the underlying invoice flow.

The Spanish Tax Agency scrutinizes export zero-ratings through cross-validation against customs exit data (SEMEGA/ESE AIS). Fraudulent or insufficient substantiation triggers: (i) immediate regularization of the undue 0% rate, converting the transaction into taxable at 21% (if domestic) or 0% with denial of the credit; (ii) late-payment interest accrual; (iii) penalty of 50% to 150% of the VAT amount evaded under arts. 191/193 LGT, increased for concealment; (iv) in criminal cases, sanction under art. 305 CP with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and six times the defrauded sum as fine; (v) retrospective clawback can extend for the 4-year statutory limitation period (art. 66 LGT), or 5 years for intra-Community transactions under special anti-fraud provisions; (vi) exclusion from CEP/VEC and the 'green channel' customs status.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain applies full capital and current account convertibility within the Eurozone and European Union under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. No prior exchange control authorisation is required for inward or outward payments. Profit remittances are unrestricted, subject only to tax compliance (withholding certification), AML source-of-funds verification by reporting banks, and post-transaction statistical declaration to the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments (for amounts above EUR 50,000 or as required). The euro is freely convertible; non-euro transfers settle in correspondent markets without requiring Banco de España approval.

Export proceeds surrender rules

No legal obligation exists in Spain to surrender export proceeds or to apply a mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted freely. The sole administrative duties are the submission of the annual/quarterly commercial transaction declaration to the DGCI (for statistical balance-of-payments purposes) and the completion of the T1 customs export declaration; proceeds repatriation timelines are contractual and not regulated.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as monetary authority and supervisor, together with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCI) of the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism for foreign investment and trade statistical declarations.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium with substantive legal constraints. A non-Spanish EMI or fintech may provide payment services in Spain only under the EU passport from its home-state regulator (for EEA EMIs) or, for third-country EMIs, after authorisation or licensing by Banco de España. EMIs cannot act as full banks, cannot grant credit, and must safeguard client funds in separate accounts; they are not viable for holding SPAC trust/escrow proceeds for public-market acquisition purposes because the escrowed acquisition war chest requires a regulated credit institution with trust-grade segregation and settlement capacity. EMIs are feasible only for low-value operational payments, not for the capital escrow rail.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Complex beneficial ownership with SPAC founders, placing agents and warrant holders

Root cause: Complex beneficial ownership with SPAC founders, placing agents and warrant holders

Defense evidence: Certified corporate tree for the Spanish SL and all upstream SPAC vehicles, individual beneficial ownership schedule (25%+ threshold declaration and ultimate controller), constitutional documents, share registry extract, sanctions/PEP screening report, and legal opinion on beneficial ownership under Spanish Corporate Enterprise Act and AML/KYC regulations.
Large escrow inflows from public market raising or investor subscription

Root cause: Large escrow inflows from public market raising or investor subscription

Defense evidence: Investor subscription agreements, broker/dealer placement statements, underwriting engagement letters, audited trust account statement or escrow attorney confirmation, source-of-funds breakdown, bank reference letters, and a sworn declaration of lawful origin of funds.
High-risk jurisdictions or counterparties (offshore financial centres, US SPAC issuers)

Root cause: High-risk jurisdictions or counterparties (offshore financial centres, US SPAC issuers)

Defense evidence: Commercial rationale memorandum with target acquisition pipeline, enhanced due diligence reports on counterparties, independent director resolutions approving the escrow mandate, evidence of no shell-bank relationships, and tax residence certificates to disprove tax evasion or aggressive avoidance.
Potential classification as a shell-bank or pass-through treasury entity

Root cause: Potential classification as a shell-bank or pass-through treasury entity

Defense evidence: Detailed business plan, personnel and substance documentation, third-party service agreements (trustee, custodian, sponsor), real office or branch lease, and board minutes demonstrating operational substance and independent exercising of control.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Inbound equity or investor funds must be routed to a Banco de España-registered credit institution through the SWIFT network using an explicit purpose code (e.g. for subscription to SPAC equity / overseas direct investment). The Spanish bank will require the foreign investor's identity, source-of-funds documentation, the completion of the Foreign Investment Statistical Statement (or subsequent post-investment declaration to the DGCI), and compliance with EU sanctions screening. Transfers above EUR 10,000 are subject to bank-documented AML profiling; wire instructions should reference the Spanish SL, its legal entity identifier 549300ES_SL, and the specific escrow mandate, avoiding third-country shell intermediary jurisdictions.Trade and acquisition disbursements are cleared primarily by SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for payments to identified sellers/investors and by documentary or standby Letters of Credit (with UCP600 rules) for commercial transactions. For large M&A consideration payments, high-value TARGET2/EBA SEPA settlement is the intra-EU rail, while USD disbursements clear through correspondent banks in New York or via euro-dollar TARGET2. All outbound wires require the same AML/CFT evidence pack and the use of the original order institution, never a third-party paying agent, unless expressly disclosed and approved by the compliance officer.Vanilla FX forwards (deliverable) executed with an authorised EU bank under ISDA/EMIR-cleared master agreementsNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to the extent the counterparty is an authorised credit institution or investment firm, with no prohibited speculative netting for non-financial treasuryCross-currency swaps for conversion of acquisition proceeds and future target cash flows, subject to EMIR margin and reportingForeign exchange options (OTC or exchange-traded) for hedging planned M&A settlement exposures, only on a documented treasury-risk basis

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium with substantive legal constraints. A non-Spanish EMI or fintech may provide payment services in Spain only under the EU passport from its home-state regulator (for EEA EMIs) or, for third-country EMIs, after authorisation or licensing by Banco de España. EMIs cannot act as full banks, cannot grant credit, and must safeguard client funds in separate accounts; they are not viable for holding SPAC trust/escrow proceeds for public-market acquisition purposes because the escrowed acquisition war chest requires a regulated credit institution with trust-grade segregation and settlement capacity. EMIs are feasible only for low-value operational payments, not for the capital escrow rail.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate. Certain qualifying newly incorporated entities may apply a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse rules.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, EU directives, and tax treaties.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the deadline moves to the next business day under the applicable electronic-filing rules.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. Large taxpayers and entities using the net-tax-base method follow the applicable electronic filing and payment calendar. A taxpayer with prior-period net turnover exceeding EUR 6 million is generally subject to the minimum payment-on-account rules.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the normal filing month is November.

Deadline: · Frequency:

The country-by-country report is generally submitted within 12 months after the end of the reporting fiscal year. The notification is generally due within the statutory corporate tax return period.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Spain does not use a single threshold for all transfer-pricing documentation. A Spanish taxpayer is generally required to maintain a local file, subject to simplified documentation and exemptions, for controlled transactions. The master-file obligation generally applies where the consolidated net turnover of the group is at least EUR 45 million. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Modelo 232 reporting thresholds also apply separately. Certain transactions with the same counterparty and category may be exempt from Modelo 232 where the statutory EUR 250,000 aggregate threshold and other conditions are satisfied; the exemption does not eliminate arm's-length or documentation obligations.

Economic substance scope: Spain has no separate regime identical to the UAE or Cayman Islands Economic Substance Regulations. Substance is nevertheless required under Spanish anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership principles, EU anti-tax-avoidance rules, the principal-purpose test in treaties, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, and the place-of-effective-management test. A Spanish SPAC or acquisition vehicle should maintain Spanish directors with genuine decision-making authority, appropriate personnel or outsourced functions, records, bank controls, board minutes, commercial rationale, risk assumption, and operational capacity. A registered address, nominee director, bank account, and pass-through expenses alone are inadequate substance.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate tax return

Statutory sanction: Administrative tax penalties commonly range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to the tax, late-payment interest, and collection costs. Tax fraud becomes a criminal offense where the defrauded tax quota exceeds EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax period. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, subject to aggravated-offense rules.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto directors may incur civil and tax liability where they intentionally participate, negligently fail to prevent the infringement, or cause the company to breach its obligations. Criminal conviction may include disqualification from public office or employment. Personal imprisonment is not automatic and requires individual criminal responsibility.
VAT fraud and fictitious invoicing

Statutory sanction: Repayment of improperly claimed VAT, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 100% or more depending on concealment and fraud. Serious cases may constitute criminal tax fraud where the statutory quota threshold is exceeded.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable where they ordered, approved, or knowingly tolerated fictitious invoicing. Criminal imprisonment, fines, and disqualification may apply to responsible individuals.
Transfer-pricing manipulation

Statutory sanction: Tax adjustments, denial of deductions, withholding-tax assessments, late-payment interest, and documentation or valuation penalties may apply. Failure to maintain required documentation can trigger statutory fixed and transaction-linked penalties, with increased exposure where the adjustment causes a tax shortfall.

Director personal liability: Directors are not automatically liable for a pricing adjustment but may face liability for deliberate concealment, false documentation, abusive arrangements, or failure to maintain legally required controls.
Withholding-tax failure

Statutory sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, and withholding-agent penalties. Treaty relief can be denied retroactively where the recipient lacks entitlement or the arrangement is abusive.

Director personal liability: Directors may become jointly or subsidiarily liable where they caused the failure, acted fraudulently, or failed to remit withheld amounts. Withholding funds for personal or group use can create severe civil and criminal exposure.
Shell company and lack of economic substance

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may disregard the arrangement under conflict-in-application or simulation rules, deny deductions and treaty benefits, recharacterize income, impose tax, interest, and penalties, and refer fraudulent conduct for criminal investigation.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil, tax, insolvency, and criminal liability if they knowingly implement a sham structure. A separate Spanish economic-substance filing regime does not protect an entity lacking genuine operations.
AML, terrorist financing, and beneficial-owner concealment

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements may result in public or private reprimands, monetary penalties that can reach the higher of statutory fixed amounts, EUR 10 million, or a percentage of annual turnover where applicable, and possible authorization or management restrictions. Suspicious transactions may require reporting to SEPBLAC.

Director personal liability: Directors and compliance officers may be sanctioned personally where they authorized, tolerated, or failed to prevent the breach. Deliberate money laundering may result in imprisonment, fines, professional disqualification, and confiscation.
Market abuse and unauthorized public offering

Statutory sanction: Administrative sanctions may include substantial fines, public statements, trading or management prohibitions, and liability for investor losses. Criminal market-abuse offenses may carry imprisonment and fines where statutory elements are satisfied.

Director personal liability: Directors, sponsors, officers, and advisers may incur personal administrative, civil, and criminal liability for misleading disclosures, manipulation, or intentional regulatory evasion.
Insolvency and asset-stripping

Statutory sanction: Transactions may be rescinded, assets recovered, and directors ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency deficit in a culpable insolvency proceeding. Civil damages, creditor claims, and criminal insolvency offenses may also arise.

Director personal liability: The insolvency court may classify the insolvency as culpable and impose disqualification from managing assets of another person, loss of rights against the insolvency estate, restitution, damages, and deficit liability. A travel ban is not an automatic tax sanction but may arise from judicial measures in exceptional insolvency or criminal proceedings.
Accounting and corporate-law violations

Statutory sanction: Registry closure, accounting penalties, tax reassessment, shareholder or creditor claims, auditor consequences, and possible criminal liability for false accounting may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for losses caused by breach of diligence duties, may be disqualified in insolvency, and may face criminal sanctions where false accounting or document fraud is proven.
Unlawful dividend or profit repatriation

Statutory sanction: Recipients may be required to repay unlawful distributions, and the company may claim damages. Tax authorities may recharacterize the payment as salary, interest, service remuneration, or a hidden distribution and assess withholding tax and penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors approving unlawful distributions may be jointly liable with recipients for restitution and damages. Personal liability may extend to tax and insolvency liabilities where statutory conditions are met.
Foreign-exchange, payment-rail, and sanctions breach

Statutory sanction: Transactions may be blocked or confiscated, bank relationships terminated, and administrative or criminal sanctions imposed under applicable sanctions, AML, and payment regulations.

Director personal liability: Responsible directors and officers may face personal fines, criminal prosecution, asset confiscation, and management disqualification. Liability depends on knowledge, authorization, control, and applicable sanctions law.
